verdicts.reason: Source task26_t222 directly shows opening a product URL, clicking '#tab-label-reviews, #tab-label-reviews-title', reading page text, and regex-parsing repeated review blocks into title, rating, body, reviewer name, and posted date. The proposed primitive preserves that site-specific acquisition/parsing and returns typed review records, while excluding the workflow's task-specific service-complaint filtering and answer selection.

Source task126_t159 directly supports a site search primitive: it opens the shopping homepage, fills the search box with a query, clicks Search, enumerates 'li.product-item' cards, reads '.product-item-link' and '.price', and converts price text to numbers. The proposed method keeps only this reusable site acquisition/parsing core and returns typed product records, excluding the workflow's Canon/photo-printer filtering and min/max aggregation.

Source task313_t134 directly demonstrates navigating from the homepage footer 'Contact Us' link to the contact page, reading visible body text, and applying a phone-number regex. The primitive is site-scoped, returns typed output as a list of phone number strings, and does not claim unsupported task interpretation beyond extraction.

Source task320_t160 directly demonstrates site-specific authentication at '/customer/account/login/' with selectors login[username], login[password], and 'Sign In', then navigating to 'My Orders', iterating 'table tbody tr', and extracting each row's 'View Order' href. The primitive appropriately keeps this authenticated acquisition core and returns typed row-level records (row_text, detail_url, and order_number when identifiable) without overclaiming unsupported structured subfields or doing task-specific selection/summing.

Source task320_t160 directly shows opening each order detail URL, reading page text, checking that the order number, canceled status, a displayed full date text, shipping amount, and grand total appear on the page, and extracting the grand total with regex. The proposed primitive narrows to that reusable detail-page parsing, returns typed fields, and correctly excludes task-specific choice of which orders to inspect and summing totals across orders.
